t: You're looking at the Old Bailey, formally the Central Criminal Court of England and Wales, named after the street it stands on in the City of London. It is one of several buildings that house the Crown Court. It was designed by Edward William Mountford, an architect noted for his Edwardian Baroque style, who also designed town halls in Sheffield, Battersea and Lancaster. He served as President of the Architectural Association, and he died young, at fifty-two, which was described as a loss to the front rank of the profession.
